passages.note: Bill details page: Wesco is the first-named House sponsor of the Indiana RFRA; this page prints the digest, not the enacted provision.
House third-reading roll call: Wesco voted Yea on final passage of this single-subject bill; 31 Nay of 94 voting, so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled act text: a general strict-scrutiny exemption reaching all statutes, ordinances and regulations, with "person" defined to include individuals and for-profit entities.

rows.reasoning: Wesco sponsored SB 101 (2015) in the House and voted Yea on its third reading; the enrolled act bars a governmental entity from substantially burdening "a person's exercise of religion, even if the burden results from a rule of general applicability" unless it meets a compelling-interest and least-restrictive-means test. That is a general exemption statute reaching "all governmental entity statutes, ordinances, resolutions, executive or administrative orders, regulations, customs, and usages", with "person" defined to include individuals and for-profit entities, which matches "protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs" rather than the narrower "protect religious freedom while ensuring it doesn't override anti-discrimination protections in employment and housing" or the religious-organisation autonomy of the top rung.
